Not a die (would turn avhv.t-class files into CRASH days before R1, per fable-answers-s318.md §1). docs/not-supported.md gained "## `tie` on an ARRAY or HASH [INTERIM — announced, not silent; scalar tie works]" and quotes the current text. STILL OPEN: real aggregate tie needs the boxed-aggregate data model (E5-era, Fable writes the design; DO NOT START). Revisit die-vs-support then.
=== MEASURED s473t6a (#1501 ROUND 8, the tie trio as ONE decision) ===

Three t/op files are ONE fact each and the fact is this task.  Measured on
2ac855aa, `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1`:

  t/op/tiehandle.t   perl 67/0  PCL 12/32, 23 rows never produced  = 56 blessed
  t/op/tiearray.t    perl 75/0  PCL 26/29, 20 rows never produced  = 50 blessed
  (t/op/tie_fetch_count.t is a SCALAR tie and is NOT this task -- see #1813.)

WHAT THE RUNTIME HAS: `p-tie` builds a `p-tie-proxy` only when its first
argument IS A BOX.  An ARRAY or HASH arrives RAW (a bare vector / hash-table)
and a FILEHANDLE arrives as a glob, so both take the
`%p-warn-aggregate-tie` arm: one stderr line and the container is left untied.
The constructor names TIEARRAY / TIEHASH exist in `p-tie` but are reached only
when the box HOLDS a vector or hash-table.  So it is not that individual
methods are missing -- there is no proxy for them to hang on (DECIDED s473h:
"#1429 is NOT a missing flag read -- `tie @array` does not exist at all").

THE METHOD INVENTORY THE TWO FILES NEED, for whoever implements the model:
  tied ARRAY  (t/op/tiearray.t): TIEARRAY FETCH STORE FETCHSIZE STORESIZE
      EXTEND EXISTS DELETE CLEAR PUSH POP SHIFT UNSHIFT SPLICE DESTROY UNTIE,
      plus the $NEGATIVE_INDICES class variable (#1429).
  tied HANDLE (t/op/tiehandle.t): TIEHANDLE PRINT PRINTF WRITE READLINE GETC
      READ EOF CLOSE BINMODE FILENO SEEK TELL OPEN DESTROY UNTIE.

A ROW CAN BE MISSING RATHER THAN FAILING: tiehandle.t has NO aborted form --
its 23 missing rows are assertions written INSIDE the tie methods (PRINT,
WRITE, READLINE), which never fire because the tie is dropped.  tiearray.t's
20 are behind one abort, the #1429 NegIndex block.

Every one of the 106 rows now carries a cause in
`baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` citing `NS:tie on an ARRAY or HASH` and this
task; the not-supported entry's s467 note already names the FILEHANDLE case.

=== THE DESIGN (Fable, s501, 2026-09-30) -- "EMPTY SHELL + SIDE TABLE".  NOT LAUNCHED: the USER decides (a feature-sized batch with a hot-path risk).  An agent builds from this section; brief ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/s501t/prompt.md ===
WHAT IT BUYS: three everyday rows (modules/Tie-Hash-Array-Scalar, programs/tied-scalar-hash, modules/Sys-Hostname-Env-English through core Env.pm), t/op/tiearray.t (50 blessed rows), every CPAN module that ties a container (Tie::File, Tie::IxHash, Env, Tie::RefHash, Tie::Memoize ...).  TIEHANDLE is a DIFFERENT representation question (a handle is a glob / fd-stream) and stays out: its own task.

THE FACTS THE DESIGN RESTS ON (read off cl/pcl-runtime.lisp on main 77212b1f):
  * an ARRAY is a bare adjustable vector, a HASH a bare hash-table; boxed aggregates (s455) changed the ELEMENTS, not the containers, so there is still no header to hang a proxy on -- the "waits for boxed aggregates" sentence at the top of this task is answered: they did not bring one.
  * `(p-tie @a "Class" ...)` already hands the runtime the CONTAINER OBJECT itself.
  * the element read fast arms have a MISS branch that costs nothing when it is not taken: p-aref = `(if (< idx (length arr)) <svref> *p-undef*)`, p-gethash = `(if found <value> *p-undef*)`.
  * tied SCALARS work through two chokepoints (unbox -> FETCH, box-set -> STORE) on a `p-tie-proxy` held in the box.

THE REPRESENTATION:
  1. A tied container stays THE SAME LISP OBJECT, EMPTIED.  Identity is what makes the tie visible through every alias perl has -- `\@a` taken before the tie, `tie @$ref`, `@_`, a glob / symbolic name (`tie @PATH` from inside Env.pm).  Rebinding the variable to a proxy object would reach none of those.
  2. Its tie lives in a SIDE TABLE: a weak (`:weakness :key`), EQ hash table container -> record {tie object, kind, the SAVED contents it had when tied (perl hides them while tied and `untie` brings them back), the each/keys iterator state}.  A global COUNT of live ties (`sb-ext:defglobal`, a fixnum: read without a TLS lookup) guards every lookup: `(and (plusp COUNT) (gethash c TABLE))`.  A program that never ties pays the COUNT test and nothing else.
  3. EMPTY is the trick: on an empty shell every element fast path MISSES, so the tie test rides in the miss branch that already exists.  An untied in-range read costs exactly what it costs today.

WHERE THE TEST GOES -- the CENSUS is the agent's first deliverable (every runtime function AND macro expansion that reads or writes a user container: about 47 `maphash`/`hash-table-count` sites and 26 `%p-vec-data` sites on main, plus `length` / `aref` / `gethash` / `vector-push-extend` on a container), classified:
  (a) element READ       -> in the miss branch (free)
  (b) array element WRITE -> the in-range store cannot happen on an empty shell; the test sits in the EXTENSION path
  (c) hash element WRITE  -> `(setf gethash)` has no miss branch: ONE COUNT test before the store.  THIS IS THE COST -- measure it first (below)
  (d) whole-container ops -> one COUNT test at entry: length / `$#a` (FETCHSIZE / STORESIZE), push pop shift unshift splice, exists delete, clear and list assignment (CLEAR + STORE / EXTEND), keys values each (FIRSTKEY / NEXTKEY), scalar(%h) (SCALAR, else perl's fallback), list-context flatten, slices, join / sort / map / grep / reverse arguments, `local`, foreach
  (e) emitted RAW shapes   -> every Kind-A emission that touches a container's storage (foreach-raw, foreach-range, elem-setf, the `:arrays t` runs, L7's copy reads) goes through a runtime macro: its expansion gets the entry test.  A shape that cannot take it is DENIED for a variable the same file ties BY NAME (extend VarAnnotator's scalar `tie-target` gate, line ~335 / ~562 / ~1692, to `tie @name` / `tie %name` -- ONE predicate) and must still be right for a container tied ELSEWHERE, which is what the entry test is for.
  Rule 12: a container op that does not know what to do with a tied container DIES naming itself -- never reads the empty shell as "no elements".  (Reading the shell is the silent wrong this design must not create: the census table carries a column "what happens on a tied container", and "empty answer" is not an allowed entry.)

ELEMENT ALIASES: `for (@tied) { $_ = 1 }`, `map`/`grep` over it, `\$tied[0]`, `f($tied{k})` with `$_[0] = ...` -- perl hands out a magical element (PVLV) whose read is FETCH(key) and whose write is STORE(key, v).  PCL: a fresh box holding an ELEMENT PROXY {tie object, key}, a second kind beside `p-tie-proxy`, served by the SAME two chokepoints.  Probe perl first for how many FETCHes each shape performs (`$h{a}++` = 1 FETCH + 1 STORE; `"$h{a}$h{a}"` = 2): tie_fetch_count.t-style rows are part of the acceptance, and a double FETCH is a visible behaviour (#1813 has the scalar side).

METHODS (call what perl calls; a missing method dies perl's way -- Tie::Array / Tie::Hash / Tie::StdArray / Tie::StdHash are CORE MODULES and load as they are, they supply the defaults):
  ARRAY  TIEARRAY FETCH STORE FETCHSIZE STORESIZE EXTEND EXISTS DELETE CLEAR PUSH POP SHIFT UNSHIFT SPLICE UNTIE  (+ $NEGATIVE_INDICES, #1429)
  HASH   TIEHASH  FETCH STORE EXISTS DELETE CLEAR FIRSTKEY NEXTKEY SCALAR UNTIE
  DESTROY: not called (USER ruling, permanent).
  `tied(@a)` / `tied(%h)` answer the object; `untie` restores the saved contents; a re-tie REPLACES (the scalar rule); `tie` returns the object.

COST BAR, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT (the discriminating measurement): add ONLY the COUNT test to the hash store path and to the whole-container entry points of push / shift / keys / flatten (a 30-line replica), then bench `arrhash hashcopy slices sortnum mapmulti intloop strcat textproc` interleaved against the base with a control pair, on a quiet box.  If any control row is slower than the noise band, STOP and bring the numbers back -- the alternative placements (a COUNT test only in the functions' SLOW arms plus a compile-time deny for same-file ties, accepting that a container tied in ANOTHER file and written through a fast store arm is not seen) are a ruling, not an agent's call.

PHASES, each its own commit with probes (perl -> base -> tree) and inverse-verified guard rows:
  1. HASH: the record, the COUNT, tie / tied / untie, every hash op of the census.  Acceptance: programs/tied-scalar-hash `same`; a probe table with Tie::StdHash subclasses that LOG every method call, the log compared with perl's line by line (the order and count of FETCH / STORE / FIRSTKEY / NEXTKEY calls is the semantics).
  2. ARRAY: the same for arrays.  Acceptance: modules/Tie-Hash-Array-Scalar `same`; t/op/tiearray.t before / after, rows read in both directions.
  3. Env: `use Env qw(HOME @PATH)` -- core Env.pm ties `$HOME` (a scalar BY NAME through a glob) and `@PATH`.  Measure what stops it after phases 1-2; fix at the layer the measurement names.
  Bars: the full sweep (a cl/ change), companion op/tie*.t op/tiearray.t op/tie_fetch_count.t op/local.t op/each.t op/hash.t op/array.t op/push.t op/splice.t lib/Tie/*.t `--jobs 1` before / after, corpus-diff (the VarAnnotator gate changes emission only in files that tie a container: list them), the bench A/B above on the final tree, everyday +2 to +3.


=== DONE (s501t, 2026-10-01 .. 10-04; resumed s503-s506 by fresh agents) ===
Built as designed: a tied ARRAY/HASH stays the same Lisp object, EMPTIED; the tie lives in a weak EQ side table guarded by a defglobal count (normative ir-spec 2.4a; record docs/tie-aggregates.md: census of sites, perl method-call table, the named log differences).  Phases 1 HASH, 2 ARRAY, 3 Env (`tie ${EXPR}` -> p-cast-$-box).  Step 0 (count test cost) inside a byte-identical control band.  Later fixes: %p-flatten-arg-values tie arm (copying/signature subs), p-cast-$-box referent + vivify (op/gmagic.t), %p-when-tied-kind one-kind rule (op/avhv.t), s505 review F1 (element proxy FETCHing a reference = that reference), F2 (boolean of a tied hash = truth of SCALAR), F3 (lib/Config.pm path_sep).
Numbers: guard Pl/t/tie-aggregate-01.t 128 rows (126 operations, 116 log-identical to perl, 10 differ in the log only, results identical); sweep TOTAL 18714 -> 18728 (sweep5.log, GATE clean, drops 5 = census); companion tie.t 17/78 -> 53/42, tiearray.t 26/29 -> 70/5, tiehash.t 20/7 -> 27/0 OK, gmagic 50/2 -> 61/3, sort 183/22 -> 185/20, magic 176 -> 179 pass, hash 8/7 -> 10/5; tiehandle 11/32 unchanged; ir-conform 345-tie passes; bench: no row above the control band; EVERYDAY 108 -> 110 of 122 (Tie-Hash-Array-Scalar, tied-scalar-hash).
